name: CA-15
label: Safe D

model.rationale: The D+26 district, Mullin's incumbency, and his roughly $820,000 raised against an underfunded Republican challenger all point to an easy Democratic hold, and Polymarket prices a Mullin win at about 95%. With no contrary polling or ratings, the fundamentals-based margin near D+27 stands.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or unusually low-turnout special dynamics could narrow the margin, though a Republican win remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

overview:
Kevin Mullin, the Democratic incumbent, advanced to the general election in a Bay Area district that leans Democratic by 26 points. He has raised about $820,000 and holds a substantial cash advantage, while Republican challenger Charles Hoelter has shown little fundraising activity and no outside spending has materialized on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and money, all of which favor Mullin heavily. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 95%. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with an expected margin in the mid-to-high twenties.
